pages.hook: Portland, Oregon, is known for food carts and for restaurants with many vegetarian dishes. Learn the words that help you choose food with no meat.
pages.polite: Ask **Do you have vegetarian dishes?** and **Is there meat in it?** Then say **Thank you, that’s perfect.**

mythfact.s: A vegetarian does not eat meat.
mythfact.why: Many vegetarians still eat eggs, milk and cheese.

mythfact.s: Vegetarian and vegan mean exactly the same thing.
mythfact.why: Vegans also avoid eggs, milk, cheese and honey.

mythfact.s: Many US menus mark vegetarian dishes with a letter like “V”.
mythfact.why: A small V or a leaf symbol is a common sign.

mythfact.s: Portland is a city in Oregon.
mythfact.why: There is also a city called Portland in Maine.

mythfact.s: Restaurants in the USA never offer a veggie burger.
mythfact.why: A veggie burger is a common option on menus.

decode.why: The (V) dishes are the vegetarian ones.

opts: What you eat or can’t eat
decode.why: It asks about diets and allergies.

compare.br: In Brazil, “sem carne” can be a surprise in a churrascaria, but vegetarian options are growing, with “prato vegetariano” at many places.
compare.us: In the USA, restaurants often mark vegetarian and vegan dishes, and servers are used to the question “Is there meat in it?”
compare.tip: Say what you don’t eat: “I don’t eat meat or fish.”
compare.ask: Do you know a vegetarian dish from your country? Say it in English.

quiz.q: You want to ask about meat. You say…
quiz.why: Is there… in it? is natural.

quiz.q: You don’t eat meat. You say…

quiz.why: It is a burger without meat.

pages.title: Reading quest — No meat, please! · part 1
text: My friend Carlos lives in **Portland**, and he doesn’t eat meat or fish. When we go to a restaurant, he always asks, “**Do you have vegetarian dishes?**”

Last Saturday, we went to a small restaurant. The server said, “Yes, we do. **The pasta is vegetarian.**” Carlos asked, “**Is there meat in it?**” “**No meat**,” she said. “Just tomato and cheese. **We have a veggie burger too.**” Carlos smiled. “**I’ll have the pasta**, please.” “**Good choice!**” she said.
My order was different. I had chicken and rice, and a glass of water. We shared a big salad: lettuce, tomato, cucumber and carrots. We said, “**Great idea!**” and “**Yum!**”

tf.why: “We have a veggie burger too.”

tf.why: The writer had chicken and rice.

pages.title: Reading quest — No meat, please! · part 2
text: After lunch, we went to the supermarket. Carlos wanted some vegetables, and I wanted flowers for my mother. I thought of the song “Supermarket Flowers” by Ed Sheeran, from 2017. It is a gentle song about love for a family member, and it is named after simple flowers from a supermarket.
In the evening, I thought about our day. It is easy to eat with friends who have a different diet. You just ask a question, listen to the answer, and **enjoy your meal**.
